source.before: Brain scientists set up "gladiator style" cage matches for mice — and found that simply observing fighting matches can rewire a mouse's brain to resemble those who actually fought.
source.highlight: We set this up to look a little bit like a gladiator arena, so the mouse is kind of above the two mice fighting on a platform.
source.after: Annegret Falkner is an associate professor at the Princeton Neuroscience Institute. … The paper is published in the journal Nature.

source.highlight: NASA is looking for astronauts to live and work on the Moon
source.after: If you have dreams of going to the moon, you now have a chance. NASA is accepting applications for those interested in becoming an astronaut. The candidates selected to be astronauts would not only test spacecraft but would also live and work on the moon in a future moon base, said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman in a statement released on Saturday.

source.before: There are currently 32 active astronauts in NASA's astronaut corps. Since NASA missions began in the 1960s, the agency has selected 370 people to train as astronauts, according to the agency.
source.highlight: The applicant process is extremely competitive. Out of more than 8,000 applicants for NASA's last astronaut class, only 10 candidates were selected.
source.after: While any U.S. citizen can apply and there is no official age restriction, applicants will need to have a master's degree in a STEM-related field such as engineering or math.
